answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond, then randomly assign bonded agents to audit one another’s signed work. If an audit proves a claim false, the offender’s bond is slashed and split among the auditors; honest agents recover theirs. A Sybil cannot gain influence merely by minting names: each new identity needs scarce capital, and coordinated fake agents risk losing it when sampled. Signed records anchor the evidence, while a cipher can protect private audit details; even an orchard of identities must pay for each seat.
